compensating.why: hop 2 binds through the mapper's ObjectReader for the type
hop 3 re-reads the tree into a new tree before passing it on
hop 4 binds with a copy of the mapper

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides how a tree becomes a value: returned as it is, unwrapped from a POJO node, or bound by reading it with the mapper. Hops 1-4 pass the receiver, the tree and the type along unchanged and return the gold's result (hop 1 only maps an I/O exception that is not a processing exception to IllegalArgumentException). Once the gold binds a tree that already is of the requested type, the result is a new, equal node, and no caller can recover the original instance from it. The gold's javadoc promises a conversion of the tree into a value of the type; the Jackson convention for a conversion is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc says treeToValue is functionally equivalent to convertValue(n, valueClass), whose javadoc says conversion happens only if needed and a value already of the requested type is returned as is; ObjectMapper._convert does that step in production (Object.class excluded), as does FromStringDeserializer.deserialize for an embedded value. TestBeanConversions::testConvertUsingCast pins the same-instance result on the sibling path; TestConversions::testTreeToValueWithPOJO (a wrapped value returned as is), TestConversions::testTreeToValue and TestTreeTraversingParser::testDataBind (ordinary trees bound) pass through the chain.
